en: This observance of the multitude of sufferings is merely the ritual for breaking one's fast; this is but a dark day in the midst of the surging essence of great bliss,
while I am engaged in the praise of the Lord, who is heavy with the scorching of the uneven arrows [of Māra] by surpassing all others.
The mind, free from fear, reflects [the truth] perpetually. // 1 //
Having reflected upon his own self, the worshipper then reflects upon the conduct worthy of praise; thus, in the act of praise, he manifests duality as its sole object.
And when his own self has been fully reflected upon at the time of knowing all objects, it is as follows:
In this world, I am constantly engaged in your praise without any effort.
One who possesses the cognition of existing entities cannot have an unreflected-upon self;
for even the notion that "the self is unreflected-upon" does not occur without the process of reflection.
Moreover, this self is Śiva, the single essence in which all manifesting entities shine forth; therefore, I am He.
With a heart inclined toward your praise, he is eternally blissful. // 3 //
O Heart, that omniscience which was attained by you through the various sequences of wandering through births and so forth,
has now clearly become manifest within your speech, its radiance having become the very path for the expansion of your awakening.
Having obtained it, now recite this hymn of praise to the Lord.
Shaking off this state of existence situated on the path of bondage and cherished [by the ignorant],
and having made it a source of aesthetic relish by burning away all duality with the sacrificial fire of infinite praise,
he drinks in all phenomena with the impetuous force of the unfolding majesty of his own manifold self-expansion.
O Giver of Boons, being intoxicated with these, I am happy. // 5 //
O Lord, whose manifold power is renowned through abundant sovereignty— if the wondrous conduct of the Blessed One dwells within the heart,
then how could one compose a hymn? And yet, one does so spontaneously because of that very [conduct].
For the attainment of identity with Śiva, bowing to Śiva is the primary means. // 6 //
Apart from its blazing form, its radiant cooking, its burning, and its manifestation, no other body whatsoever can be established for fire; therefore,
if I praise the rays of consciousness according to their respective natures, by that very act, he (Fire) would be praised.
There is no other manifestation whatsoever of the Supreme Lord. // 7 //
In that state where there is a manifold beginning and all fixed rules have dissolved, there is indeed a flavor (*rasa*) characterized by supreme fullness due to the absence of limitation;
it is a union with self-luminous manifestations, consisting of the single essence of all states of existence, and is not opposed by anything.
The supreme consciousness possesses qualities worthy of the priceless through the floods of Dharma.
O Giver of Boons, in such forms as these, your body indeed shines forth in various ways within this world that is your own portion; yet for the Blessed One, it remains free from all differentiation.
It is precisely to praise this very reality that my heart, my speech, and the activity of my external senses are now engaged.
May my impetuous zeal never be abandoned. // 9 //
It is from you alone— the ocean of consciousness whose inner light flashes— that there naturally flows the impulse for the spreading of various multitudes of waves;
these very [phenomena] possess a radiance flashing forth as the nature of creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
The simultaneous arising, passing away, and manifestation of the moon, the sun, and fire. // 10 //
Therefore, the power of the All-pervasive Lord— which abides in various and non-various sequences, as well as in their opposites— never undergoes any differentiation whatsoever.
Thus, on this level, that which is indeed your state is called "Akula" (the Unmanifest).
O Lord Bhairava, become one-pointed within my heart. 11.

From that completely full [reality], O Vata, through the expansion of Your own will, You cause Your own power— which is delightful with the great surge of aesthetic flavor— to undergo differentiation;
this priceless sovereignty of Yours is truly wondrous.
Praising the power of existence, I am free from fear and become one with Śiva.
This form of yours, O Blessed One, is full of power;
because of the absence of sequential succession, it forcibly dissolves the measurement of time—
whether through the power of the mind, or through speech, or through the circles of the senses, or externally through jars and other objects.
I shall constantly assume that form simultaneously. // 13 //

O Lord, manifesting the unfolding of the stages upon that ground, You perpetually extend the differentiation of Your own powers within Your own Self; thus, You assume a threefold form consisting of action, knowledge, and will, which possess the majesty of maintenance, dissolution, and great emanation.
May I be one whose heart is intent upon resting in meditative concentration. // 14 //
O Lord Bhairava, this creation of yours— which was formerly dissolved here in the nature of fire,
which now manifests as it moves toward the longing for supreme expansion, and which partakes in the abundant splendor of both fire and moon— is beautiful through its contact with the moon.
May that which is called creation shine eternally within my mind. // 15 //
When the objective aspect has been cast outward and becomes tasteless due to the lack of intense savoring, if you then passionately take on a state of redness toward that very same [aspect],
then may the Goddess Raktā surely grant me [union] within all your states of being.
Free from disgust toward those who have entered into a gathering formed through the sequence of drinking blood. // 16 //
O Lord, when you— having destroyed the turbulence of the waves— manifest the non-difference of all states in order to abandon external activity and dwell upon the noble ground of consciousness,
then that Goddess effects the destruction of your worldly existence.
May she always bring about the destruction of my worldly existence. // 17 //
Desiring to bring peace through the dissolution of the world,
you have now promulgated both injunction and prohibition— known as the affliction of your own doubt—
out of your own impetuosity; yet, having thus created Yama, you once again shatter that very doubt.
May this Great Goddess shatter my fear of cyclic existence. // 18 //
O Lord, when the flood of doubt has dissolved, when sovereign power is fully restored, when worldly custom has passed away, and when the constraints of scripture have lost their force—
then the one whose essence is greed is everywhere eager to swallow the infinite stream of enjoyments.
May that which is called Saṃhārā strike at the portion of duality within my heart. // 19 //
Thus, when the power of duality has been instantly shattered by the Goddesses,

this state of the Mothers, whose life-breath is conceptual construction, shines forth fully; therefore, having contemplated within one's own heart that aspect of withdrawal which consists of the state of abiding, [one attains it].
May the Blessed Lady, who brings about the dissolution of death, be gracious toward me.

Thus, these three powers, having attained their respective stations within the sequence of the six cakras by virtue of the expansion of their own inherent glory, produce through their successive unfolding a manifold state of worldly existence. From these [powers], [the world arises].
May my heart be inclined toward the goddesses, and may I be free from fear. // 21 //
He blocks this ground that causes the terror of the fear of worldly existence, and he also effects this state consisting of the intense melting of the singular essence of awakening;
thus, having both blocked and dissolved the series of impurities, he brings about this melting.
She, who follows conduct according to her will, shines within my heart. 22.

She who forcibly withdraws into herself the entire essence of the sun— along with its activity, intellect, and senses— which has attained the status of a limited means of knowledge within its own sphere, by means of her own respective radiance;
she is that [Śakti] who possesses the station of stability.
May she, drawing me away from the fear of worldly existence, bring about my separation from it. // 23 //
May the Supreme Goddess—who, free from succession, repeatedly establishes her entire stream of consciousness within herself;
who is filled with a vast mass of great rays of light streaming forth from the infinite interior;
and who is gracious and full of noble devotion—bestow upon me divine bliss.
May it adorn the path of the heart. // 24 //

When the means of knowledge (pramāṇa) has dissolved due to the power of the splendor shining in the state of Śiva, and when the limitation consisting of the body, vital breath, and so forth— which comprises the state of the limited, conditioned subject—
attains the stage of dissolution along with its adjunct of time, then that Goddess [who is]...
May she be auspicious for me. // 25 //
The consciousness known as Light, devoid of succession, having completely dissolved from the state of the Void, flows forth as a total veil;
then, within the inner core, through the subsiding of its impetus, it becomes Mahākālī by virtue of being beyond succession.
May this [practice] be for me as I pass all time. // 26 //
Then, in that Goddess who abides in the state of supreme perfection, those whose minds are firmly established quickly sever the succession [of mental constructs] and, out of intense delight,
perceive the means of knowledge (*pramāṇa*), the knower (*mātṛ*), and the object of knowledge (*miti*)— indeed, this entire world— as abiding [within her].
Embracing it, let it take refuge in this consciousness of mine. // 27 //
I bow to that Lord, the possessor of power, in whom those all-pervading powers abide within His own nature which is free from restraint.
Known as Manthāna, it is the sole essence of the world. // 28 //
O Lord, if you grant me your favor upon hearing these compositions of praise for the flood of rays of your own power,
then by that [favor], may all people quickly [attain liberation].
May you bring about the complete pacification of the mass of darkness by the rays of your own teaching. // 29 //
In the sixty-sixth year, on the ninth day of the dark fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa,
Śiva was praised by me, Abhinavagupta.
Thus ends the *Kramastotra* composed by the venerable teacher Abhinavaguptapāda.
